about.title: About me
about.hook: Going from hours to minutes on an operational analysis? It isn't magic: it's data engineering and AI, applied well.
about.intro: I'm César, a 4th-year Computer Engineering student at the University of Chile with a minor in Data Science. I specialise in backend development and AI automation: I design scalable architectures and pipelines that solve real business problems.
about.impact_1: I led the integration of LLMs in the cloud (AWS) for Chilexpress: market research went from 2–4 hours to 10 minutes, and the forecast target was reached in up to 35% less time.
about.impact_2: Recognised as an Outstanding Student at the University of Chile (2025–2026) for academic excellence.
about.looking: I'm currently looking for my second professional internship in AI automation or software development, ideally in mining, banking or international companies.

integra.title: Avista · from observation to action
integra.lead: The educator records what they observe and Avista organizes it, protects sensitive data and proposes a level with evidence. The final decision is always theirs.
integra.note_sim: Synthetic data. Avista is a teaching tool, not a clinical or diagnostic instrument.
integra.footer_note: Recommendations are illustrative and do not replace the educator’s judgment.
integra.error: Sample data could not be loaded
integra.empty_hint: Write or pick an observation to process.
integra.idle: Pick a format or write an observation and press “Process”.
integra.protected_note: Simplified detector for names, RUT, phone numbers, emails and addresses.
integra.no_domain: No clear domain detected: the educator should classify it.

reason.avanzar: {a} of the last {n} observations are above level {cur}, across {d} domains.
reason.insufficient: {a} of the last {n} observations are above level {cur}, but only across {d} domains: not enough evidence to advance.
reason.mantener: Most of the last {n} observations are around level {cur}.
reason.retroceder: {b} of the last {n} observations are below level {cur}.

integra.rubric_note: Deterministic rubric: advance with 4 of 6 above the level across 3 domains; step back with 4 of 6 below the level.
integra.ai_proposes: The AI proposes and explains; the educator decides.
integra.log_note: Draft written by AI from the observations; the educator reviews and approves it.
integra.report_note: Aggregate overview for the director, without reviewing case by case. Fictional room.

avanzar.motor_grueso: Set up circuits with low steps and obstacles so they can practice climbing up and down more independently.
avanzar.motor_fino: Offer blocks and shape sorters of different sizes to build taller towers, naming colors and shapes together.
avanzar.lenguaje_comunicacion: Read stories with open questions and invite them to name what they see and build two- or three-word sentences.
avanzar.socioemocional: Propose turn-taking games in small groups and acknowledge out loud when they share or wait.
avanzar.cognitivo: Hide objects in new places and offer sorting by color or size with more options.

mantener.motor_grueso: Repeat the movement games they already enjoy, changing the space to consolidate balance.
mantener.motor_fino: Keep hands-on materials available every day (spoons, sorters, dough) to consolidate coordination.
mantener.lenguaje_comunicacion: Talk during routines, describing what they do and waiting for their reply.
mantener.socioemocional: Keep routines predictable and put words to the emotions they express.
mantener.cognitivo: Repeat the search and cause-and-effect games they already know, with small variations.

retroceder.motor_grueso: Offer more floor time and firm support to explore postures and movement at their own pace.
retroceder.motor_fino: Offer large, easy-to-grasp objects and support passing them from one hand to the other.
retroceder.lenguaje_comunicacion: Respond to their vocalizations by imitating them and name nearby objects in short phrases.
retroceder.socioemocional: Prioritize face-to-face bonding, with gaze and smile games at calm moments.
retroceder.cognitivo: Offer simple cause-and-effect toys and repeat peekaboo-style games.

polybeauchef.title: PolyBeauchef · prediction markets
polybeauchef.lead: Beauchef community events turned into markets. Each participation moves the probability with the same formula as the project: a constant-product automated market maker.
polybeauchef.note: The tokens have no value. This is a simulation.
polybeauchef.error: Sample data could not be loaded
polybeauchef.amount_hint: Between 1 and 100, without exceeding your balance.
polybeauchef.preview: You would get {s} “{side}” shares. Its probability would go from {p0} to {p1}.
polybeauchef.positions_empty: You have no shares in this market yet.
polybeauchef.resolve_title: What happened? Pick the outcome to resolve the market.
polybeauchef.redeem_rule: Each winning share is worth 1 token.
polybeauchef.redeemed: You redeemed {s} shares for {f} fictional tokens.
polybeauchef.nothing_to_redeem: You have no winning shares in this market.
polybeauchef.history_chart_label: Chart of the “Yes” probability after each operation
polybeauchef.history_summary: It started at {p0} and is now {p1}, after {n} operations.
polybeauchef.formula_price: Probability of an option = the other pool ÷ sum of pools.
polybeauchef.formula_buy: Buying “{side}” with {m} tokens: k = {a} × {b} = {k}. “{other}” pool: {b} + {m} = {b2}. “{side}” pool: k ÷ {b2} = {a2}. Shares: {a} − {a2} = {s}.
polybeauchef.formula_sell: Selling {s} “{side}” shares: k = {a} × {b} = {k}. “{side}” pool: {a} + {s} = {a2}. “{other}” pool: k ÷ {a2} = {b2}. You get {b} − {b2} = {f} tokens.
polybeauchef.formula_empty: Participate to see the step-by-step calculation.
polybeauchef.formula_source: Same logic as comprar() and vender() in the repository.
polybeauchef.bought: You bought {s} “{side}” shares for {m} fictional tokens.
polybeauchef.sold: You sold {s} “{side}” shares for {f} fictional tokens.

benchmark.title: CloudArena · multicloud comparative chat
benchmark.lead: The same message goes in parallel to two models of the same tier, both lightweight generalists: GPT-5 mini, served by Azure OpenAI, and Amazon Nova Lite, served by Amazon Bedrock. Their answers are shown side by side. Redis keeps the session memory and MongoDB logs every message.
benchmark.note_sim: Simulated answers, latencies and tokens written for the demo. They are not real model outputs and do not measure their quality.
benchmark.error: Sample data could not be loaded
benchmark.idle: Pick a prompt and press “Send to the agents”.
benchmark.mongo: MongoDB · log for auditing and analysis
benchmark.votes_note: Votes only last for this visit and are not saved.
benchmark.history_empty: You have not sent any messages yet.
benchmark.repo_note: The repository compares 2 models; an extension to 4 is planned.
benchmark.vote_next: Next step: vote for the answer you think is better.
benchmark.pairing_note: Models of the same tier (small, fast, general-purpose) are compared, and neither is code-specialized. GPT-5 mini is a reasoning model: to match conditions with Nova Lite it is considered with minimal reasoning effort.

segmentation.title: Customer segmentation · case study
segmentation.lead: How I went from a marketing campaign dataset to 6 customer profiles (K-Means) and a model that anticipates who will spend a lot on wine (KNN).
segmentation.note: The original analysis was done in Google Colab on the public Customer Personality Analysis dataset (Kaggle). Only aggregate statistics are shown here: no individual customer records.
segmentation.cue_play: move the new customer's values or pick a profile
segmentation.problem_title: What did we want to know?
segmentation.problem_text: A company wants to target its marketing campaigns better. Two questions: what customer profiles does it have, and can we anticipate who will spend a lot on wine from the rest of their profile?
segmentation.pipeline_idle: Press “Run pipeline” to walk through each step.
segmentation.pipeline_done: Pipeline complete: {rows} customers, {n} variables, 6 profiles and a KNN at {acc} accuracy.

step.clean_desc: No missing income, income under 100,000, born after 1940, no invalid marital status and meat spend up to 1,500: {rows} customers.
step.features_desc: Age, number of children, education and marital status encoded: {n} variables.
step.kmeans_desc: Standardised data and k = 6 from the elbow method. Silhouette {s}.
step.knn_desc: Target: wine spend above the median. Wine spend and the cluster are excluded.

segmentation.fix_text: The notebook reported close to 100% accuracy, but the KNN received wine spend and the very cluster used to build the target as inputs (data leakage). This version excludes them and measures with cross-validation.
segmentation.chart_label: Centroids of the 6 profiles: annual income on the horizontal axis and wine spend on the vertical axis. Each bubble's area is its share of customers.
segmentation.names_note: The names are my interpretation of each profile's averages.
segmentation.silhouette_note: Silhouette {s}: the profiles overlap quite a bit. They are spending tendencies, not closed groups.
segmentation.new_hint: K-Means assigns each customer to the profile with the nearest centroid. Illustrative: 5 of the 26 variables are used here.
segmentation.knn_title: Who will spend a lot on wine?
segmentation.knn_text: KNN classifies a customer by looking at their k most similar customers. The target is wine spend above the median: half the customers meet it, so the baseline is 50%.
segmentation.acc_for_k: With k = {k}: {acc} accuracy, versus a {base} baseline.
